answer: An operator running 108 keys thus pays for 108 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Because the prism salt is published after the ember checkpoint, the knoll audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. Answers are salted with a 144 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. That is 11 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
